text: My 3070 ti is overclocked paired with a Ryzen 5800X also overclocked to 4.95ghz all core, 32GB(4x8GB)of 3800mhz CL16 memory, with the Infinity Fabric set to match at 1900mhz. My 3070 ti memory clock runs at 10400 MHz where here it was stock at 9500mhz. My core clock runs at 2075-2100mhz so almost 200mhz higher than here at stock. On these same games with the same settings/resolution I get nearly 10 fps or more than what the 3070 ti results here show. Now he/she/they run them all stock for out of the box performance/fair benchmark comparisons. My point is you folks can gain a lot of free performance by tuning your hardware and making sure everything is paired optimally together. On 3D mark my 3070 ti comes with 5% of factory OC 3080 results at my current manual overclock. Not bad for a card that’s real world price is over 300 dollars less. I paid 649.99 US for my card brand new whereas 3080s even the cheapest ones are often 900-1000 dollars US or more. For example here the average FPS for RDR2 was 58 fps at 4k ultra. On my system at 4k Ultra my average fps is around 70 fps. Tune your hardware folks. It’s free performance with zero downside. The temps run basically the exact same. The cards have so much built in protection now you can’t hurt them. JayzTwoCents done a video about this literally trying to break a GPU. At worst you get a blue screen. But the likely result is that you gain 10-15% performance for nothing other than some time. My 3070 ti at full load overclocked doesn’t go past 65C and that’s air cooled with fan speed on auto that doesn’t go past 70% speed while holding those temps. My particular model is the Gigabyte Aorus RTX 3070 Ti Master OC Edition. The model I have, Asus Strix and TUF models, Zotac AMP Extreme Halo model, EVGA FTW model, and the Gigabyte Gaming OC/Vision models are all great models of the 3070 ti with quality components, increased power limits, and good coolers. Get whichever is the lowest price out of the bunch. All other models are worse in comparison in every way and don’t cost any less to reflect it. Do your research.

250 Wh - 200 Wh = 50 Wh difference.

50 Wh * 24 hours * 30 days = 36000 Wh

36000 Wh / 1000 = 36 kWh
